key_themes: Portfolio optimization strategy focused on four pillars: shedding high-cost bulk deposits (~INR 38,000-40,000 crores), reducing treasury by INR 15,000 crores, eliminating IBPC portfolio (INR 20,000 crores), and converting low-yielding portfolio (INR 10,000 crores) to long-term loans
Strong asset quality improvement with GNPA and NNPA reduction, SMA2 at lowest level of INR 4,285 crores (above INR 5 crores), and 95% of corporate book rated BBB and above
Digital transformation and technology leadership - ranked 2nd in EASE agenda among PSBs, received 4 Technology Awards including Best Bank Tech Award, implementing AI and robotic process automation
RAM (Retail, Agriculture, MSME) segment showing robust growth: 11.50% overall, 21.67% in Retail, 19.75% in Agri, while maintaining quality focus in corporate book
Project MUSKAAN initiative for operational streamlining, ease of doing business, risk mitigation, and cost reduction through bottom-up approach and process improvements
Strategic shift from bulk deposits to retail deposits and CASA to protect margins, resulting in 21.85% Y-o-Y reduction in high-cost bulk deposits
Focus on sustainable growth with calibrated balance between top line expansion and bottom line strength, while maintaining asset quality
Portfolio rebalancing toward higher-yielding retail, agriculture, and MSME (RAM) segments from 55% to target 58%, reducing lower-yielding corporate exposure
Significant improvement in asset quality metrics with gross NPA declining 107 bps Y-o-Y to 3.29% and net NPA down 43 bps to 0.55%
Strong capital position with 17.07% capital adequacy and 14.37% CET-1 ratio, among the best in industry
management_outlook: Positive economic environment with India expected to achieve ~7.4% GDP growth in Goldilocks phase (high growth, low inflation), supported by regulatory measures including 125 bps repo rate cut and 100 bps CRR reduction
NIM protection strategy working effectively - maintained NIM at 2.76% (increased from September quarter) despite 125 bps rate cut, compared to 2.91% in December 2024
Confident about managing ECL transition with minimal impact - only INR 4,200-4,300 crores additional provision required on netting basis, expecting credit cost to remain in 20-40 bps range
Strong pipeline with INR 24,000-26,000 crores of sanctioned loans pending disbursement, indicating sustained momentum in loan origination
Bank crossed INR 10 lakh crores advances milestone for first time, achieved highest Return on Assets at 1.35% and highest RoE, with CASA ratio improving 140 bps quarter-over-quarter
Aspires to achieve 9-10% growth on both asset and liability sides going forward, targeting system-level or better growth quarter-on-quarter
Plans to maintain CD ratio between 78.5-80% and increase CASA by 1-1.5% coupled with retail term deposits rather than bulk deposits
Confident about protecting and improving NIMs going forward by shifting from treasury to loan book and reducing low-yielding corporate exposures
Expects convergence with industry growth rates to accelerate, with sequential quarterly growth matching or exceeding system levels
Projects full impact of bulk deposit reduction strategy to materialize in current and subsequent quarters
analyst_concerns: Other interest income elevated at INR 206 crores vs typical INR 100 crores in recent quarters - management clarified INR 198 crores is RIDF recovery
Expected run-rate impact of draft ECL (Expected Credit Loss) norms on ongoing credit costs beyond transition impact
Sustainability of 4% Q-o-Q loan growth given ongoing portfolio optimization and mixed changes within corporate book
Quantum of SMA2 accounts below INR 5 crores (management indicated ~INR 24,000-25,000 crores but promised exact numbers separately)
Deposit growth lagging at 3.36% vs advances growth of 7.13%, though management explained strategic reduction of high-cost bulk deposits
Bank's loan growth at 5% Y-o-Y significantly lags system growth of 11%, with questions about timeline to reach parity with industry
Mismatch between stated strategy and actual numbers - cost of deposits only down 5 bps despite bulk deposit cuts, while yield on advances fell 16 bps
Elevated standard asset provisioning of Rs. 880 crores in the quarter, with questions about nature (ECL, SMA, or prudential provisioning)
Net interest income registered quarter-on-quarter de-growth despite management's margin protection strategy
Concerns about bulky upgradation in the quarter and whether there was associated provisioning reversal from lumpy accounts
guidance_statements: Credit cost expected to remain in the range of 20-40 basis points even after ECL implementation, with minimal increase from current run-rate
Provisioning Coverage Ratio maintained at more than 95%, providing adequate buffer for asset quality management
INR 24,000-26,000 crores of sanctioned loans in pipeline for disbursement, supporting near-term loan growth momentum
Cost of funds and deposits showing steep reduction trajectory due to strategic reduction of INR 38,000-40,000 crores high-cost bulk deposits
Capital ratios and liquidity ratios are comfortable and well within regulatory requirements to support growth plans
Target 9-10% growth on both assets and liabilities going forward, with aspiration to exceed system-level growth quarter-on-quarter
Aim to increase RAM (Retail, Agriculture, MSME) portfolio from current 55% to 58% while reducing corporate exposure from 45%
Maintain CD ratio between 78.5-80% levels with focus on increasing CASA by 1-1.5% and retail term deposits
Target retail to bulk deposit mix of 75:25 and RAM to corporate lending ratio of 55:45 (moving to 58:42)
NIM maintained at 2.67% with confidence in protecting and potentially improving margins going forward

concall_themes: Portfolio optimization strategy focused on four pillars: shedding high-cost bulk deposits (~INR 38,000-40,000 crores), reducing treasury by INR 15,000 crores, eliminating IBPC portfolio (INR 20,000 crores), and converting low-yielding portfolio (INR 10,000 crores) to long-term loans
Strong asset quality improvement with GNPA and NNPA reduction, SMA2 at lowest level of INR 4,285 crores (above INR 5 crores), and 95% of corporate book rated BBB and above
Digital transformation and technology leadership - ranked 2nd in EASE agenda among PSBs, received 4 Technology Awards including Best Bank Tech Award, implementing AI and robotic process automation
RAM (Retail, Agriculture, MSME) segment showing robust growth: 11.50% overall, 21.67% in Retail, 19.75% in Agri, while maintaining quality focus in corporate book
Project MUSKAAN initiative for operational streamlining, ease of doing business, risk mitigation, and cost reduction through bottom-up approach and process improvements
Strategic shift from bulk deposits to retail deposits and CASA to protect margins, resulting in 21.85% Y-o-Y reduction in high-cost bulk deposits
Focus on sustainable growth with calibrated balance between top line expansion and bottom line strength, while maintaining asset quality
Portfolio rebalancing toward higher-yielding retail, agriculture, and MSME (RAM) segments from 55% to target 58%, reducing lower-yielding corporate exposure
Significant improvement in asset quality metrics with gross NPA declining 107 bps Y-o-Y to 3.29% and net NPA down 43 bps to 0.55%
Strong capital position with 17.07% capital adequacy and 14.37% CET-1 ratio, among the best in industry
analyst_concerns: Other interest income elevated at INR 206 crores vs typical INR 100 crores in recent quarters - management clarified INR 198 crores is RIDF recovery
Expected run-rate impact of draft ECL (Expected Credit Loss) norms on ongoing credit costs beyond transition impact
Sustainability of 4% Q-o-Q loan growth given ongoing portfolio optimization and mixed changes within corporate book
Quantum of SMA2 accounts below INR 5 crores (management indicated ~INR 24,000-25,000 crores but promised exact numbers separately)
Deposit growth lagging at 3.36% vs advances growth of 7.13%, though management explained strategic reduction of high-cost bulk deposits
Bank's loan growth at 5% Y-o-Y significantly lags system growth of 11%, with questions about timeline to reach parity with industry
Mismatch between stated strategy and actual numbers - cost of deposits only down 5 bps despite bulk deposit cuts, while yield on advances fell 16 bps
Elevated standard asset provisioning of Rs. 880 crores in the quarter, with questions about nature (ECL, SMA, or prudential provisioning)
Net interest income registered quarter-on-quarter de-growth despite management's margin protection strategy
Concerns about bulky upgradation in the quarter and whether there was associated provisioning reversal from lumpy accounts
management_outlook: Positive economic environment with India expected to achieve ~7.4% GDP growth in Goldilocks phase (high growth, low inflation), supported by regulatory measures including 125 bps repo rate cut and 100 bps CRR reduction
NIM protection strategy working effectively - maintained NIM at 2.76% (increased from September quarter) despite 125 bps rate cut, compared to 2.91% in December 2024
Confident about managing ECL transition with minimal impact - only INR 4,200-4,300 crores additional provision required on netting basis, expecting credit cost to remain in 20-40 bps range
Strong pipeline with INR 24,000-26,000 crores of sanctioned loans pending disbursement, indicating sustained momentum in loan origination
Bank crossed INR 10 lakh crores advances milestone for first time, achieved highest Return on Assets at 1.35% and highest RoE, with CASA ratio improving 140 bps quarter-over-quarter
Aspires to achieve 9-10% growth on both asset and liability sides going forward, targeting system-level or better growth quarter-on-quarter
Plans to maintain CD ratio between 78.5-80% and increase CASA by 1-1.5% coupled with retail term deposits rather than bulk deposits
Confident about protecting and improving NIMs going forward by shifting from treasury to loan book and reducing low-yielding corporate exposures
Expects convergence with industry growth rates to accelerate, with sequential quarterly growth matching or exceeding system levels
Projects full impact of bulk deposit reduction strategy to materialize in current and subsequent quarters
